Introduction to Earth Science: Earth science
The study of Earth's systems, materials, and place in space
Geology
The branch of Earth science studying solid Earth and its history
Meteorology
The study of the atmosphere and weather
Oceanography
The study of the oceans and their processes
Geosphere
The solid rock and metal portion of Earth
Hydrosphere
All of Earth's water in liquid, solid, and vapour form
Atmosphere
The layer of gases surrounding Earth
Biosphere
The zone of Earth containing all living organisms
Uniformitarianism
The principle that present-day processes explain past geology
Scientific model
A simplified representation used to explain a natural system
Topographic map
A map showing elevation using contour lines
Contour interval
The elevation difference between adjacent contour lines
Minerals and Rocks: Mineral
A naturally occurring inorganic solid with a definite crystal structure
Silicate mineral
A mineral built around silicon and oxygen tetrahedra
Mohs hardness scale
A ranking of mineral scratch resistance from talc to diamond
Cleavage
The tendency of a mineral to break along flat planes
Fracture
Irregular breakage in a mineral lacking cleavage
Streak
The colour of a mineral's powder, a reliable identification test
Igneous rock
Rock formed from cooled and solidified magma or lava
Intrusive igneous rock
Rock cooled slowly underground with large crystals
Extrusive igneous rock
Rock cooled quickly at the surface with fine crystals
Sedimentary rock
Rock formed from compacted and cemented sediments
Metamorphic rock
Rock changed by heat and pressure without melting
Foliation
The banded texture produced by directed pressure in metamorphism
Rock cycle
The continuous transformation among the three rock types
Plate Tectonics: The theory that Earth's lithosphere is broken into moving plates
Wegener's hypothesis that continents were once joined and moved apart
The supercontinent that existed roughly 250 million years ago
The rigid outer shell of crust and upper mantle
The weak, partly molten mantle layer plates slide over
New crust forming at mid-ocean ridges and moving outward
A boundary where plates move apart and new crust forms
A boundary where plates slide past one another
One plate sinking beneath another into the mantle
Circulating mantle material that drives plate motion
A stationary mantle plume creating volcanoes as a plate passes over
Symmetric magnetic stripes on the seafloor confirming spreading
Earthquakes and Volcanoes: Earthquake
Ground shaking caused by sudden release of stored energy
Focus
The point underground where an earthquake actually begins
Epicenter
The point on the surface directly above the focus
Fault
A fracture in rock along which movement occurs
P wave
The fastest seismic wave, compressional and able to travel through liquid
S wave
A slower shear wave that cannot pass through liquid
Surface wave
The slowest seismic wave, responsible for most damage
Seismograph
The instrument that records seismic waves
Richter scale
A logarithmic measure of earthquake magnitude
Moment magnitude scale
The modern measure based on total energy released
Shadow zone
The region where S waves are absent, revealing a liquid outer core
Shield volcano
A broad, gently sloped volcano built by fluid basaltic lava
Composite volcano
A steep cone of alternating lava and ash, often explosive
Viscosity and eruption style
High silica producing thick lava and violent eruptions
Weathering, Erosion, and Soil: Weathering
The breakdown of rock in place at Earth's surface
Mechanical weathering
Physical breakup of rock without chemical change
Frost wedging
Rock splitting as water freezes and expands in cracks
Chemical weathering
Alteration of rock's mineral composition by reaction
Hydrolysis and oxidation
Reactions with water and oxygen that decompose minerals
Erosion
The transport of weathered material by wind, water, or ice
Deposition
The settling of transported sediment in a new location
Soil horizon
A distinct layer within a soil profile
Humus
Decayed organic matter that enriches topsoil
Soil profile
The vertical sequence of horizons from surface to bedrock
Mass wasting
Downslope movement of material under gravity
Desertification
The degradation of once-productive land into desert
Glacial erosion
Ice carving U-shaped valleys and depositing moraines
Earth's History and Geologic Time: Determining the order of events without exact ages
Determining numerical age, usually by radioactive decay
In undisturbed layers, older rock lies beneath younger rock
A feature cutting across rock is younger than the rock
A gap in the rock record representing missing time
A widespread, short-lived fossil useful for dating layers
The time for half a radioactive sample to decay
Using carbon-14 to date organic material up to roughly 50,000 years
The division of Earth's history into eons, eras, and periods
The vast span covering roughly the first four billion years
A rapid loss of a large fraction of Earth's species
About 4.6 billion years, established by radiometric dating
Oceanography: The concentration of dissolved salts in seawater
A layer of rapid temperature decrease with depth
The shallow submerged edge of a continent
An underwater mountain chain where new crust forms
A deep, narrow depression formed at a subduction zone
Wind-driven ocean flow affecting the upper water layer
A large circular current system in an ocean basin
The rise of cold nutrient-rich water toward the surface
Deep global flow driven by differences in temperature and salinity
The periodic rise and fall of sea level caused by gravity
An unusually large tidal range at new and full moon
A reduced tidal range at first and third quarter moon
The bending of waves as they approach shore at an angle
The Atmosphere and Weather: Troposphere
The lowest atmospheric layer, where weather occurs
Stratosphere
The layer above the troposphere containing the ozone layer
Air pressure
The force per unit area exerted by the weight of the atmosphere
Humidity
The amount of water vapour present in air
Relative humidity
Water vapour present as a percentage of the maximum possible
Dew point
The temperature at which air becomes saturated
Coriolis effect
The deflection of moving air caused by Earth's rotation
Front
The boundary between two air masses of different properties
Cold front
A boundary where cold air advances, often bringing storms
Warm front
A boundary where warm air advances, bringing steady precipitation
Cyclone
A low-pressure system with inward, rising air
Anticyclone
A high-pressure system with sinking air and fair weather
Jet stream
A fast, narrow band of high-altitude wind steering weather systems
Isobar
A map line connecting points of equal air pressure
Climate and Climate Change: Climate
The long-term average pattern of weather in a region
Latitude and climate
Sunlight striking at lower angles produces cooler climates
Maritime effect
Oceans moderating nearby temperatures year round
Rain shadow
The dry region on the leeward side of a mountain range
Greenhouse effect
Atmospheric gases trapping outgoing infrared radiation
Greenhouse gas
A gas such as carbon dioxide or methane that absorbs infrared
Albedo
The fraction of sunlight a surface reflects
Ice core record
Trapped air bubbles providing a history of past atmospheres
Milankovitch cycles
Variations in Earth's orbit and tilt that pace ice ages
El Nino
A periodic Pacific warming that shifts global weather patterns
Positive feedback loop
A change that amplifies itself, such as melting ice lowering albedo
Ocean acidification
Seawater becoming more acidic as it absorbs carbon dioxide
Climate proxy
Indirect evidence such as tree rings used to reconstruct past climate
Astronomy and the Solar System: Solar system
The Sun and all objects gravitationally bound to it
Nebular hypothesis
The theory that the solar system formed from a collapsing gas cloud
Terrestrial planet
A small, dense, rocky inner planet
Jovian planet
A large, low-density gas or ice giant
Astronomical unit
The average Earth-Sun distance, about 150 million kilometres
Kepler's first law
Planets orbit in ellipses with the Sun at one focus
Kepler's second law
A planet sweeps equal areas in equal times, moving faster when closer
Kepler's third law
Orbital period squared is proportional to average distance cubed
Asteroid belt
The rocky debris zone between Mars and Jupiter
Comet
An icy body that develops a tail when approaching the Sun
Meteor and meteorite
A streak of light in the atmosphere versus a fragment that lands
Retrograde motion
Apparent backward planetary motion explained by relative orbital speeds
Lunar phases
The changing sunlit fraction of the Moon seen from Earth
Solar and lunar eclipse
The Moon blocking the Sun versus Earth's shadow falling on the Moon
Stars and the Universe: Star
A self-luminous ball of gas powered by nuclear fusion
Nuclear fusion
Light nuclei combining to release energy, powering stars
Luminosity
The total energy a star radiates per second
Apparent magnitude
How bright a star appears from Earth
Absolute magnitude
How bright a star would appear at a standard distance
Hertzsprung-Russell diagram
A plot of luminosity against temperature revealing stellar classes
Main sequence
The band on the H-R diagram where stars fuse hydrogen
Red giant
A swollen, cooler late stage of a Sun-like star
White dwarf
The dense remnant core left by a low-mass star
Supernova
The explosive death of a massive star
Neutron star
An extremely dense remnant made almost entirely of neutrons
Black hole
An object whose gravity prevents even light from escaping
Light-year
The distance light travels in one year
Redshift
The stretching of light from receding objects, evidence of expansion
Big Bang theory
The model that the universe expanded from an extremely hot dense state
Cosmic microwave background
Faint leftover radiation supporting the Big Bang
